title: the headless critic exits 0 when it asked nothing: the Swift pack arms no rule and a Rust file reached only by clippy-armed rules prints ok, so a judge's critic leg reads nothing judged as clean
body:
Found by intent-ic's positive controls after issue 0646 and raised by molt-vc on 2026-10-25; measured by vc the same hour in a fresh linked worktree with planted files; filed by vc, in 3.2.7.

## What happens

A judge's critic leg (decision 79 on vc's board) reads the headless critic's exit code, and the runner exits 0 in two cases where it judged nothing:

- `intent critic swift --files <f>` arms 0 of 6 rules headless (all six declared unanswerable), prints `no swift rule was asked of any of the 1 file(s) given`, and exits 0 on a file holding a force unwrap and a `try!`. Every Swift critic leg run on the desk on 2026-10-25 judged nothing and was read as clean.
- `intent critic rust --files <f>` on a file whose only defects belong to the three clippy-armed rules prints `ARMED but NOT RUN HERE ... IN-RS-CODE-001(clippy) IN-RS-CODE-002(clippy) IN-RS-CODE-005(clippy)` and then `ok: no rust findings at severity >= warning across 1 file(s)`, exit 0. The reach itself is sound: from inside a linked worktree a planted `Result<u8, String>` fires IN-RS-CODE-004 exactly as from the main checkout (ic's planted unwrap and `todo!` were clippy-armed rules, not a reach defect).

## Expected

A judge can tell "nothing was judged" from "judged and clean" by the exit code alone, and a Swift file can be judged headless for the rules that have a greppable proxy.

## The fix, specified (vc, 2026-10-25)

1. The runner answers a distinct exit code when no rule was asked of any file given (every rule unanswerable, or every file outside every armed rule's reach), say 4, documented beside 0, 1, 2 and 3 in `intent/docs/critics.md` and wherever the exit codes are stated once after ST0088; the pre-commit gate maps 4 to pass with the runner's line printed, since a file no rule reaches must not block a commit; a judge leg maps 4 to red with its reason unless that file class is expected to be unreached. The `ok:` line is not printed when nothing was asked; the existing `no <lang> rule was asked` line is the answer.
2. The Swift pack gains greppable proxies for the rules that have one (a force unwrap `!` outside `!=` and prefix `!`, `try!`, `as!`, `fatalError(` outside a `precondition`-style guard, the pack's own judgement on each), so `intent critic swift --files` arms them headless, with a positive control per proxy in the critic tests and a negative that a clean file stays clean; rules with no proxy stay declared unanswerable.
3. Decision 79 is amended: every critic leg opens with a known positive per language from the same directory the leg runs in, and a leg whose runner answers 4, 2 or 3 is red with that reason.

Arms: the runner's exit-code arms in intent-cli's critic tests (no rule asked gives 4; one finding gives 1; the gate's mapping); the Swift proxies' positive and negative controls; `critic_surface.rs` and the dispatch arms following. Judge: the intent-cli suite, the critic bats, fmt, clippy, the critic leg itself with its positive. XS to S. Owner: cc, after 0647.
